01 / About

Curious mind.
Creative perspective.

A visual sensibility shaped by design, a problem-solving approach shaped by data, and a growing interest in the decisions that turn an idea into a useful product.

“I’m drawn to the space where an idea becomes visible, understandable and meaningful to the people it is meant for.”

I'm Pankaja, pursuing a B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) at Malla Reddy College of Engineering. My interests sit across creative communication and analytical problem-solving. I’m especially drawn to the way visual choices influence what people notice, understand and remember — whether that is a brand, a publication or an event.

My college experience has given me opportunities to create visual identities, design newsletter covers and selected internal pages, develop event and promotional creatives, and contribute to student-led communication initiatives. These experiences have taught me to think beyond the artwork itself: to consider its audience, purpose, context and the message it needs to carry.

Alongside design, I’m genuinely interested in Product Management. I’m curious about how teams identify user needs, make trade-offs, shape product direction and bring different perspectives together to build useful experiences. I see design, communication and data-informed thinking as complementary skills in that process.

03 / Selected projects

Ideas made
tangible.

A selection of work across visual identity, institutional communication and applied technology. The projects vary in scale and subject, but each has involved translating a brief or problem into something clearer, more usable or more engaging.

01 / Brand exploration

TalentSpark

TalentSpark is a placement-preparation platform concept initiated by a college alumnus. Its focus is helping students practise through aptitude and technical quiz questions. The brief called for a visual identity that could sit naturally within an education and career-readiness context.

I independently developed multiple logo directions, exploring how the name and the platform’s learning-and-opportunity context could be expressed visually. The supplied concept shown here is one direction from that exploration. The identity remains in progress: the concepts have not been finalised or approved.

My role · Independent logo concept exploration
02 / Healthcare identity

CareNest

CareNest was developed as a hackathon project centred on healthcare and medical support for pregnant women. I created the project logo independently, aiming for a visual language that feels supportive and approachable while signalling a healthcare context.

My role · Logo design
03 / Institutional communication

From Gratitude to Greatness

Created at the Head of Department’s request for a New Year event, this banner was designed to represent the department and communicate the event’s spirit. The HOD used the creative, which was also featured on the college’s official website — a meaningful example of student design being taken into an institutional setting.

04 / Academic technical project

Plagiarism Detection using AI

Developed a web application to detect plagiarism in text documents and flowchart images. Implemented NLP similarity detection using LCS-based matching and OpenCV image comparison.

Achieved approximately 81.9% accuracy in detecting flowchart image plagiarism.

Python · Django · NLTK · OpenCV · NumPy · MySQL
Time-aware
Food Discovery

Hybrid recommendation system

05 / Data science project

Time-Aware Food Recommendation System

Developed a hybrid recommendation system using collaborative and content-based filtering. Evaluated models using Precision, Recall, F1-score, AUC and NDCG.

Python · TensorFlow · Pandas · NumPy · SQL
